title: Review of Family-Level Short-Term Load Forecasting and Its Application in Household Energy Management System
authors: Ma, P.; Cui, S.; Chen, M.; Zhou, S.; Wang, K.
tldr: Comprehensive review of deep learning methods for household-level short-term load forecasting and their role in home energy management systems.
problem_and_motivation: Household-level electricity load forecasting is more challenging than system-level forecasting due to the randomness and uncertainty caused by human behavior and weather changes. Existing deep learning methods need systematic evaluation to understand their strengths and weaknesses for residential energy management.
approach: Systematic literature review of deep learning-based methods for household load forecasting including RNN, LSTM, CNN, and hybrid models.
Analysis of feature extraction techniques such as wavelet decomposition, mutual information, and principal component analysis for improving prediction accuracy.
Review of adaptive learning approaches including online learning, transfer learning, and incremental learning for dynamic load patterns.
Examination of probabilistic load forecasting methods that model uncertainty in future electricity consumption.
Exploration of ultra-short-term and device-level load forecasting using bottom-up approaches.
Discussion of how household load forecasting supports scheduling and optimization in home energy management systems.
findings: LSTM-based models outperform several other machine learning algorithms in household load prediction accuracy.
Hybrid SVR-LSTM model achieved correlation coefficient R = 0.9901 for microgrid load prediction.
CNNGRU model with attention mechanism reached 92.06% accuracy in small-range load prediction.
Prediction time reduced by 75% compared to general deep learning time series prediction models.
Bottom-up appliance-level forecasting can significantly reduce forecasting errors compared to direct household-level prediction.
Online adaptive RNN methods can continuously learn from newly arrived data and adapt to new consumption patterns.

definitions.definition: Home Energy Management System — a hub connecting users with the power grid to optimize electric energy utilization.
Short-Term Load Forecasting — predicting electricity demand over hours to days ahead.
Long Short-Term Memory — a recurrent neural network architecture with memory cells for learning long-term dependencies.
Convolutional Neural Network — a deep neural network using local connections and weight sharing for feature extraction.
Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring — disaggregating total household load into individual appliance consumption.
Advanced Metering Infrastructure — smart metering systems enabling fine-grained energy data collection.
Probabilistic Load Forecasting — methods that model uncertainty in future electricity consumption predictions.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This review paper synthesizes the current state of household-level short-term load forecasting using deep learning methods. It categorizes approaches into neural network models (LSTM, CNN, hybrid), feature extraction techniques, adaptive learning methods, and probabilistic forecasting frameworks. The paper identifies key challenges including data quality issues, model overfitting with small datasets, real-time performance requirements, and the need for interpretable models. It also explores the emerging area of appliance-level and ultra-short-term forecasting enabled by smart meter deployment and IoT devices.
directly_justifies: LSTM networks with memory cells solve gradient explosion and disappearance in sequential time series prediction.
Hybrid CNN-LSTM models capture both short-term local patterns and long-term dependencies in load data.
Online adaptive learning enables models to continuously update parameters according to changing consumption patterns.
Probabilistic load forecasting captures uncertainty for better stochastic decision-making in energy management.
Bottom-up appliance-level forecasting can significantly reduce errors compared to direct household-level prediction.
limits: Review covers energy load forecasting domain, not personal finance directly.
Most cited studies use energy consumption datasets with limited generalization to financial time series.
No new experimental validation is presented as this is a literature review.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was conducted. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling and Forecasting) was flagged as most relevant, with 6.B assigned medium relevance because the paper reviews sequential time series forecasting algorithms (LSTM, CNN, hybrid models) that are transferable to financial spending data. Domain 6.A received low relevance as predictive modeling techniques are discussed but in the energy domain. Domain 4 (Landscape and Limitations) received contextual relevance for providing analogous system review context. All other domains (1-3, 5, 7-14) were considered and rejected because the paper does not address personal finance behaviors, budgeting strategies, anomaly detection, mobile design, data privacy, engagement, evaluation frameworks, savings, debt, synthetic data, or ML deployment specific to financial systems.

limitations: Review paper with no original experimental data or novel algorithm proposal.
Focus limited to energy load forecasting, not directly applicable to personal finance domains.
Most cited deep learning methods evaluated on relatively small household datasets with limited generalization evidence.
Does not address cost, scalability, or deployment challenges of deep learning models in practical settings [unacknowledged]
